newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-GRAYSON ENDS ARGENTINA'S UNBEATEN RUN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GRAYSON ENDS ARGENTINA'S UNBEATEN RUN.

text.p: NORTHAMPTON, England, Dec 10 Reuter) - Axed England fly-half Paul Grayson steered the A team to a 22-17 victory over Argentina on Tuesday.

The Northampton stand-off, dropped after kicking England to the Five Nations Championship last season with 81 points, fired a warning to current No 10 Mike Catt with five penalties and a conversion to winger Steve Hackney's 73rd minute try.
Grayson's club half-back partner, Matthew Dawson, also overlooked by England coach Jack Rowell this season, was not so fortunate.
He was carried off in the 20th minute with damaged knee ligaments and later hobbled away from the ground on crutches. It was a bruising clash in which three other England A players went off injured.

Grayson had kicked England A into a 12-5 lead just after the interval with his fourth penalty before Argentina, unbeaten in their earlier tour matches, stormed back with a brilliant try from left wing Facundo Soler in the 46th minute.
Eight minutes later they took the lead when Jose Cilley converted a penalty try awarded against the England front row.
It was Cilley's only success after earlier missing two conversions and four penalties.
Grayson put England back in front at 19-17 when he converted Hackney's try in the corner and then he had the final say in injury time with his fifth penalty.
